How Long Does a Jar of Night Cream Last? Sizes and Cost per Month

By Mohammed Nihal, founderPublished 20 October 2026Updated 16 October 20266 min read
Quick answer

Used once a night in a pea-sized amount, a 10 g jar lasts about 2 to 3 weeks, 15 g about 3 to 4 weeks, 25 g about 5 to 6 weeks and 30 g about 6 to 8 weeks. Using it morning and night roughly halves that.

  • 30 g lasts about 6 to 8 weeks at a pea nightly
  • 10 g lasts about 2 to 3 weeks
  • Avocado Night Cream costs about ₹350–₹465 a month
  • Twice-daily use roughly halves jar life

  1. How long does night cream last? Jar life by size
  2. Why the figures allow for a little more than a pea

How long does night cream last? Used once a night in a pea-sized amount, a 10 g jar lasts about 2 to 3 weeks, a 15 g jar about 3 to 4 weeks, a 25 g jar about 5 to 6 weeks and a 30 g jar about 6 to 8 weeks. Use it morning and night, or generously on the neck too, and those times roughly halve.

Below is the jar life of each size, what a month of each Mirc Glow cream really costs, and a quick way to tell whether you are using too much or too little.

How long does night cream last? Jar life by size

Jar sizeNights of useRoughly
10 gAbout 14–212–3 weeks
15 gAbout 21–283–4 weeks
25 gAbout 35–425–6 weeks
30 gAbout 42–566–8 weeks

These are typical figures for once-a-night use on the face and neck, not promises. Your own jar may last a little more or less.

Why the figures allow for a little more than a pea

A pea-sized amount for the face is about 0.4 to 0.5 g. In real life, you also put a little on the neck, some stays on your fingertips, and the last bit in the jar is hard to scoop out. Together that comes closer to half to three-quarters of a gram a night, which is what the table above is based on.

If you use cream on your face only and scrape the jar clean, it can stretch a little longer. Our guide on how much night cream to use explains how to find the right amount for your skin type and season.

What makes a jar run out faster or slower

  • Morning and night use: roughly half the jar life.
  • Neck, chest and hands: each extra area adds up quickly.
  • Winter, AC or dry skin: a second thin layer on dry cheeks can shorten jar life by a week or more.
  • Oily skin in summer: half a pea is often enough, so the jar lasts longer.
  • Sharing: two people sharing one 30 g jar will finish it in about three to four weeks.
  • Skipping nights: the jar lasts longer, but the cream works through regular use, so this is not a saving.

Cost per month of each Mirc Glow jar

Here is what each jar works out to, using its price and the jar life above. "Per month" assumes a 30-day month at once-a-night use, rounded to the nearest ₹5. The lower figure is for a jar that lasts at the longer end.

How the figures are worked out, using the 30 g Avocado Night Cream as an example: ₹649 ÷ 56 nights × 30 = about ₹350 a month if the jar lasts 8 weeks, and ₹649 ÷ 42 nights × 30 = about ₹465 a month if it lasts 6 weeks.

What the table shows:

  • The 30 g Avocado Night Cream is the lowest cost per month in our range, because it has the lowest price per gram.
  • The 10 g jar is the lowest spend up front but the highest per month among the avocado creams. It is best for patch testing, travel or a desk drawer, not as your long-term jar.
  • The 15 g and 25 g jars land close together per month, so choose between them on ingredients, not price. The 15 g is avocado and aloe vera only; the 25 g adds niacinamide and kojic acid.
  • Glutathione Cream and Glass Glow Cream cost more per month because of what is in them, not because you need more of them. The same pea-sized amount applies.

Combos are simply two or three jars, so work out each jar separately. For a wider look at price bands, see night cream price in India and avocado night cream price in India.

A quick check that you are using the right amount

  1. Write the date on the lid the day you open a new jar.
  2. After two weeks, look inside. A 30 g jar should be roughly a quarter to a third used.
  3. If it is already half empty, you are using too much. Cut back to one pea for the face.
  4. If it has barely moved after a month, you are either missing nights or using too little. Skin that feels tight by morning confirms it.

For the technique itself, see how to apply night cream.

How many jars until you see a difference?

Skin feels softer within days of starting any night cream. A more even-looking tone takes longer: skin renews roughly every 4 to 6 weeks, and most people need 8 to 12 weeks of nightly use with sunscreen every morning. That is one to two 30 g jars. Judge a cream at the end of the second jar, not halfway through the first.

Jar life vs shelf life

Finishing a jar in 6 to 8 weeks is also good for freshness. Once opened, every cream has a period after opening, shown as a small open-jar symbol such as 6M or 12M. Most people finish a jar well within that, but a half-used jar left in a drawer for months is a different story. Our guide to whether night cream expires explains the symbols and the signs a cream has gone off.

You can compare every jar size on our night cream page. Salons and resellers buying by weight can see bulk night cream.

Short answers

How long does a 30 g night cream last? About 6 to 8 weeks at a pea-sized amount once a night.

How long does a 10 g cream last? About 2 to 3 weeks of nightly use, which makes it a good size for patch testing.

Is a bigger jar better value? Usually. The 30 g Avocado Night Cream costs about ₹21.63 per gram, compared with ₹34.90 for the 10 g jar.

Why does my night cream finish so fast? Most often from using more than a pea, applying it twice a day, or adding the neck and hands from the same jar.

Should I use more cream to see results faster? No. A bigger amount does not speed anything up and can feel heavy or cause small bumps.

This is general skincare information, not medical advice. Patch test any new product, and see a dermatologist if you have a skin condition.
